subject: Subprocessor change notice — request for permission & evidence (DataBridge Solutions)
messages:
From: Paul Murphy <paul.murphy@veridiananalytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security@veridiananalytics.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Notification: new downstream subprocessor onboarding — DataBridge Solutions (logs analytics)

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Quick heads up from our side: Veridian is planning to engage a new subprocessor, DataBridge Solutions, to handle aggregated logging and analytics for the integration we run with Redwood. DataBridge will only process hashed request/response metadata and service-level logs (no raw PII or customer content).

Key details: 
- Vendor: DataBridge Solutions (data-bridge.com)
- Purpose: log aggregation, index/search for debugging and routing metrics
- Location: Ireland (AWS eu-west-1)
- Processing start requested: 2026-08-24 (we can push if you need more time)

We need permission for onward processing under our DPA and confirmation that this is acceptable under Redwood's subprocessors policy. Attached are: the updated subprocessor roster (sheet with DataBridge entry) and DataBridge's security briefing.

Asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood approve this change (or provide conditional approval) by EOD 2026-08-13?
2) Any additional evidence or SCC/DPIA info you need from us or DataBridge?
3) Any required encryption key-flow requirements (e.g., customer-managed keys) we should plan for?

I appreciate a quick turnaround — this helps our rollout schedule. If useful, happy to set a 30-min sync with security/ops.

Thanks,
Paul Murphy
Director, Platform Partnerships
Veridian Analytics

Attachments: subprocessor-roster_v3.xlsx, DataBridge-security-summary.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Paul Murphy <paul.murphy@veridiananalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Notification: new downstream subprocessor onboarding — DataBridge Solutions (logs analytics)

Thanks for the notice, Paul — sending this to our legal and security leads. A couple quick clarifying Qs (keeping it short so we can stick to your timeline):

- Confirmed processing scope: you wrote "hashed request/response metadata and service-level logs" — can you confirm there will be no customer-provided content or free-text fields in the logs? (even hashed content can be sensitive depending on how it’s derived)
- Do you have a signed DPA between Veridian and DataBridge? If not, please provide a timeline for getting a DPA in place.
- Does DataBridge have SOC 2 Type II or an equivalent attestation? If not, will they agree to controls mapping or a scoped SIG questionnaire?

Operational asks from our side to speed review: if you can provide DataBridge's SOC/SIG/CAIQ PDF or an internal security questionnaire link, plus the proposed DPA or contract template, we can triage faster. Also flag whether any keys for decrypting logs will be customer-managed versus Veridian-managed.

Cc'ing Kimberly (security) and Laura (legal) to confirm compliance scoping.

From: Paul Murphy <paul.murphy@veridiananalytics.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security@veridiananalytics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Notification: new downstream subprocessor onboarding — DataBridge Solutions (logs analytics)

Jonas — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and attaching evidence per your ask.

- Processing scope: confirmed — DataBridge will receive only indexed logging metadata (request IDs, status codes, timing metrics, anonymized endpoint hashes). No customer content, no free-text fields.
- DPA: We do not yet have a signed DPA between Veridian and DataBridge; DataBridge is prepared to sign our flow-down DPA (we've attached a proposed DPA template and a redline copy).
- Attestations: DataBridge does not currently hold SOC 2 Type II. They have completed an external security assessment and a completed vendor questionnaire; we've attached the PDF summary and a completed SIG-lite export. They have agreed to a 30-day remediation window for any critical gaps we identify.
- Key management: DataBridge will store logs encrypted at rest using AWS KMS keys owned by DataBridge (not customer-managed). They are open to a contract clause limiting access and requiring key rotation.

We uploaded a folder with the vendor questionnaire and security summary here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-veridian-vendor-evidence

If Redwood needs SCC signatures or a DPIA write-up reflecting onward transfer in the EEA, we can coordinate to produce those quickly. Proposed timeline: if Redwood can conditionally approve by 2026-08-13 we can keep the Aug 24 target; otherwise we can pause until approvals are in place.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if needed.

Paul
Director, Platform Partnerships
Veridian Analytics

Attachments: DataBridge-security-summary.pdf, subprocessor-roster_v3.xlsx, SIG-lite-export.json (attached as summary PDF)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Paul Murphy <paul.murphy@veridiananalytics.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 20:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Notification: new downstream subprocessor onboarding — DataBridge Solutions (logs analytics)

Paul — Laura from Legal here. Thanks for the materials and the Drive link. We've reviewed the summary and DataBridge's questionnaire output at a high level.

Conditional approval: Redwood can provide conditional approval for DataBridge onboarding subject to the following items being completed and agreed in writing before any production data flow to DataBridge:

1) Executed DPA (Veridian <-> DataBridge) with flow-down clauses that: 
   - Preserve Redwood's right to audit the subprocessor for processing related to Redwood-originated traffic;
   - Require DataBridge to adhere to security controls equivalent to SOC 2 (or a remediation plan acceptable to Redwood);
   - Prohibit any onward transfers outside specified EU regions without prior notice and written approval.
2) Signed SCCs (if applicable) or confirmation that Veridian will be the data exporter/controller under SCCs as required; provide final SCC execution plan.
3) A short DPIA addendum describing the risks of indexing hashed endpoints and the mitigation steps; Veridian to provide this by 2026-08-17.
4) Clarify key management expectations — if Redwood customers in scope require CMKs, we will flag that as a future requirement; for now, a contractual limitation on key access plus encryption-at-rest is acceptable.

Please update the vendor roster in your Drive folder with the executed DPA and a final evidence pack. Once the DPA is executed and the DPIA addendum is uploaded, Legal will confirm final sign-off.

If you want, we can prepare a short contract addendum template for Veridian to circulate to DataBridge — happy to draft this week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
